name: Standard Route (Southeast Ridge via Jackita Ridge / Crater Lake Trail)
approach: From the Canyon Creek Trailhead (1,900 ft) on SR 20 (32.8 mi east of Marblemount / 55.1 mi west of Winthrop), take Jackita Ridge Trail #738, fording Canyon Creek and Granite Creek near the start. The trail climbs steeply through timber via numerous switchbacks (roughly 55) gaining about 3,400 ft over 4 miles to a junction near 5,000-5,260 ft, with views opening onto Crater and Jack Mountains above timberline. Turn left/west onto the Crater Lake Trail (brushy, user-maintained) for about a mile to Crater Lake basin (~5,000-5,700 ft) below the peak's south side.
descent_text: From the summit, descend the scree/talus slopes back to the top of the crux gully and downclimb it carefully, following the same painted yellow X's/arrows and cairns used on the ascent (parties note this section is loose and exposure-sensitive both ways). Continue around the false summit's west side back onto the southeast ridge, drop into Crater Lake basin, and rejoin Jackita Ridge Trail for the descent to the Canyon Creek Trailhead, re-fording Granite and Canyon Creeks.

pitch_detail.notes: Steep switchbacking climb (~55 switchbacks) through timber from Canyon Creek TH (1,900 ft), fording Canyon Creek and Granite Creek, gaining ~3,400 ft over 4 miles to a ~5,000-5,260 ft junction.
~1 mile west on an overgrown user trail to Crater Lake basin (~5,000-5,700 ft) on the peak's south side.
Steep ~400 ft gain from Crater Lake basin onto the SE ridge, moderating near 6,800 ft; traverse around the west side of a false summit.
Loose gully near 7,600 ft with multiple cliff bands; marked by fading yellow paint X's/arrows and cairns. Reported as the route's crux — loose rock and route-finding-dependent.
Scree/talus above the gully leads to the summit plateau and remnants of the old fire lookout at 8,132 ft.

watch_out: The 3rd-class gully near 7,600 ft is the crux — loose, exposed, and easy to go off-route on without the painted markers.
Canyon Creek and Granite Creek fords near the trailhead can run high and dangerous in early season/high runoff.
The approach trail is described as brushy and overgrown past the ~5,000 ft junction toward Crater Lake.
